To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
milk from mothers of VPT infants has a higher content of macronu-trients, especially fat, protein, and lactose, and lower content of water than milk from mothers of full-term infants.
milk from mothers of VPT infants is highly variable in its macronutrient and fatty acid composition, but that the fatty acid composition of milk is not related to the gestational age of the infant.

the macronutrient composition in milk from mothers feeding very preterm infants was highly variable, and that there was no significant difference between the macronutrients composition in milk from women who delivered at 23-27 gestational weeks compared to women who delivered at <23 gestational weeks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new and innovative approaches to the analysis of the nutritional quality of milk.
the effects of milk composition and feeding on the growth and health of infants.
the effects of maternal diet and exercise on maternal and infant outcomes, and the role of maternal diet and lifestyle in the development of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of human milk for preterm and term infants is safe, but that the use of bovine milk protein-based formulas is also safe.
milk protein intake should not be limited to 2-2.5 g/kg/d, but that the optimal protein intake in preterm infants is still unknown.
there is no conclusive evidence that the content of protein and fat in the diet of mothers of VLBW infants should be different than in the diet of other mothers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the content of macronu-trients in milk from mothers with very preterm infants (VPIs) varies greatly.
the content of macronu-trients in human milk from mothers of VPI is highly variable.
the more we know about the microbiome and its interactions with the host, the less we understand it.
The main takeaway from our work is that
milk composition is highly variable, even among mothers with the same gestational age at delivery, and even within the same mothers.
we should be more cautious about the way we use the term “breast is best” in relation to preterm infants.
the macronutrient composition of milk from mothers of preterm infants is very variable.
